verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              प्रातरुत्थाय कृष्णस्तु कृतवान् सर्वमाह्निकम्। ब्राह्मणैरभ्यनुज्ञातः प्रययौ नगरं प्रति ॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Having got up (from the bed) in the morning, Krishna attended to the daily rites; and with the permission of the Brahmanas went towards the city.

verses.sanskrit: तं प्रयान्तं महाबाहुमनुज्ञाप्य महाबलम्। पर्यवर्तन्त ते सर्वे वृकस्थलनिवासिनः ॥२॥
verses.english: All those residents of Vrikasthala returned after duly informing the greatly powerful one, who was departing (for the city).

verses.sanskrit: धार्तराष्ट्रास्तमायान्तं प्रत्युज्जग्मुः स्वलङ्कृताः। दुर्योधनादृते सर्वे भीष्मद्रोणकृपादयः ॥३॥
verses.english: The of Dhritarashtra with the exception of Duryodhana, Bhishma, Drona, Kripa and others, beautifully attired went forth to (receive) him who was coming towards them.

verses.sanskrit: पौराश्च बहुला राजन् हृषीकेशं दिदृक्षवः। यानैर्बहुविधैरन्यैः पद्भिरेव तथा परे ॥४॥
verses.english: Crowds of the townsmen, o king, desirous of having a look of Hrishikesha, were there in diverse sorts of conveyances, while there were others on foot. son

verses.sanskrit: स वै पथि समागम्य भीष्मेणाक्लिष्टकर्मणा। द्रोणेन धार्तराष्ट्रैश्च तैर्वृतो नगरं ययौ ॥५॥
verses.english: He (Krishna) too having met with Bhishma who does acts without any efforts and Drona and the sons of Dhritarashtra on the way, went to the town surrounded by them.

verses.sanskrit: कृष्णसम्माननार्थं च नगरं समलङ्कृतम्। बभूव राजमार्गश्च बहुरत्नसमाचितः ॥६॥
verses.english: For paying honour to Krishna the city was well ornamented and the public roads were decked with diverse sorts of gems and precious stones.

verses.sanskrit: न च कश्चिद्गृहे राजंस्तदाऽऽसीद्भरतर्षभ। न स्त्री न वृद्धो न शिशुर्वासुदेवदिदृक्षया ॥७॥
verses.english: There was none who stayed within the house, O king, on that occasion. O bull among the race of Bharata-no woman, no aged, no child was indoors out of a desire to have a gaze of Vasudeva.

verses.sanskrit: राजमार्गे नरास्तस्मिन् संस्तुवन्त्यवनिं गताः। तस्मिन् काले महाराज हृषीकेशप्रवेशने ॥८॥
verses.english: On the public road the people with their heads bowing down on the earth were praising him in verses at that time, O great king, when Hrishikesha entered the city.

verses.sanskrit: आवृतानि वरस्त्रीभिर्गृहाणि सुमहान्त्यपि। प्रचलन्तीव भारेण दृश्यन्ते स्म महीतले ॥९॥
verses.english: The spacious mansions, filled with the ladies of rank, seemed to tremble under their weight to fall over upon the ground.

verses.sanskrit: तथा च गतिमन्तस्ते वासुदेवस्य वाजिनः। प्रनष्टगतयोऽभूवन् राजमार्गे नरैर्वृते ॥१०॥
verses.english: The steeds of Vasudeva, though swift in speed lost their motion, in the public road covered over by human beings.

verses.sanskrit: स गृहं धृतराष्ट्रस्य प्राविशच्छत्रुकर्शनः। पाण्डुरं पुण्डरीकाक्षः प्रासादैरुपशोभितम् ॥११॥
verses.english: That lotus-eyed grinder of foes entered the gray-coloured abode of Dhritarashtra graced with many palaces.

verses.sanskrit: तिस्रः कक्ष्या व्यतिक्रम्य केशवो राजवेश्मनः। वैचित्रवीर्यं राजानमभ्यगच्छदरिन्दमः ॥१२॥
verses.english: come to After traversing through the apartments of the royal abode, Keshava, the subduer of foes, came to the royal son of Vichitravirya.

verses.sanskrit: अभ्यागच्छति दाशार्हे प्रज्ञाचक्षुर्नराधिपः। सहैव द्रोणभीष्माभ्यामुदतिष्ठन्महायशाः ॥१३॥
verses.english: On the scion of the Dasharha race approaching towards him, the high-famed ruler of men, who had eyes of wisdom, along with Drona and Bhishma stood up;

verses.sanskrit: कृपश्च सोमदत्तश्च महाराजश्च बाह्लिकः। आसनेभ्योऽचलन् सर्वे पूजयन्तो जनार्दनम् ॥१४॥
verses.english: So also Kripa, Somadatta and the great king Balhika stood up from their respective seats for worshipping Janardana.

verses.sanskrit: ततो राजानमासाद्य धृतराष्ट्रं यशस्विनम्। स भीष्मं पूजयामास वार्ष्णेयो वाग्भिरञ्जसा ॥१५॥
verses.english: Then having the king Dhritarashtra of renown, the scion of the Vrishni race honoured him along with Bhishma with suitable words and without delay.

verses.sanskrit: तेषु धर्मानुपूर्वीं तां प्रयुज्य मधुसूदनः। यथावयः समीयाय राजभिः सह माधवः ॥१६॥
verses.english: Madhava, the slayer of Madhu, having done honour to them according to the usual custom, exchanged words with other kings according to their age.

verses.sanskrit: अथ द्रोणं सबाह्लीकं सपुत्रं च यशस्विनम्। कृपं च सोमदत्तं च समीयाय जनार्दनः ॥१७॥
verses.english: Janardana then addressed Balhika and the famous Drona with his son and Kripa and Somadatta.

verses.sanskrit: तत्रासीदूर्जितं मृष्टं काञ्चनं महदासनम्। शासनाद्धृतराष्ट्रस्य तत्रोपाविशदच्युतः ॥१८॥
verses.english: There in that place was a large wheat made of gold, of beautiful workmanship and ornamented with jewels, on which Achyuta took his seat at the request of Dhritarashtra.

verses.sanskrit: अथ गां मधुपर्कं चाप्युदकं च जनार्दने। उपजह्रुर्यथान्यायं धृतराष्ट्रपुरोहिताः ॥१९॥
verses.english: They, headed by Dhritarashtra, duly offered to Janardana, as was the custom, a cow, honey, curds and water.

verses.sanskrit: कृतातिथ्यस्तु गोविन्दः सर्वान् परिहसन् कुरून्। आस्ते साम्बन्धिकं कुर्वन् कुरुभिः परिवारितः ॥२०॥
verses.english: The rites of hospitality being finished, Govinda stayed there (for a short time) surrounded by the Kurus, jesting with them and exchanging words of courtesy according to his relationship.

verses.sanskrit: सोऽर्चितो धृतराष्ट्रेण पूजितश्च महायशाः। राजानं समनुज्ञाप्य निरक्रामदरिन्दमः ॥२१॥
verses.english: He, the subduer of his enemies, being worshipped and honoured by Dhritarashtra of great fame, issued out with the permission of the king.
verses.bhavadeepa: परिहसन् नर्म कुर्वन् साम्बन्धिकं धनञ्जयादिसम्बन्धहेतुकं व्यवहारम् ॥२०॥

verses.sanskrit: तैः समेत्य यथान्यायं कुरुभिः कुरुसंसदि। विदुरावसथं रम्यमुपातिष्ठत माधवः ॥२२॥
verses.english: Madhava, having exchanged greetings with the Kurus suitably in their assembly, went to the enchanting abode of Vidura.

verses.sanskrit: विदुरः सर्वकल्याणैरभिगम्य जनार्दनम्। अर्चयामास दाशार्हं सर्वकामैरुपस्थितम् ॥२३॥
verses.english: Vidura approached and worshipped Janardana of the Dasharha race and presented him every auspicious and desirable offering.

verses.sanskrit: या मे प्रीतिः पुष्कराक्ष त्वद्दर्शनसमुद्भवा। सा किमाख्यायते तुभ्यमन्तरात्माऽसि देहिनाम् ॥२४॥
verses.english: What is the use of describing the pleasure I feel, owing of my seeing you; for you are the universal soul of all embodies creatures.

verses.sanskrit: कृतातिथ्यं तु गोविन्दं विदुरः सर्वधर्मवित्। कुशलं पाण्डुपुत्राणामपृच्छन्मधुसूदनम् ॥२५॥
verses.english: Vidura, conversant with all the virtues, having finished the rites of hospitality to Govinda, asked the slayer of Madhu about the welfare of the sons of Pandu.

verses.sanskrit: प्रीयमाणस्य सुहृदो विदुरो बुद्धिसत्तमः। धर्मार्थनित्यस्य सतो गतरोषस्य धीमतः ॥२६॥
verses.english: That scion of the Dasharha race who sees everything as plainly as what he sees before his eyes, told everything in detail about the doings of the Pandavas to Khattva. Vidura was the best among the honest and learned men and he also was the dear friend and well-wisher (of the Pandavas), he was wise, honest and a man of principle, virtuous and learned in worldly profit and he felt no malice (for the Pandavas), Anrn

verses.sanskrit: तस्य सर्वं सविस्तारं पाण्डवानां विचेष्टितम्। क्षत्तुराचष्ट दाशार्हः सर्वं प्रत्यक्षदर्शिवान् ॥२७॥
verses.bhavadeepa: विदुरः पाण्डवानां विचेष्टितं तस्य तं कृष्णं प्रत्यपृच्छदित्यन्वयः । सार्धश्लोक एकं वाक्यम् । अपृच्छदिति पूर्वस्मादनुकृष्यते । प्रीयमाणस्येत्यादिषष्ठ्यौ द्वितीयार्थे ॥२६॥
